newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Photos show China has not beefed up Spratlys - Ramos.
newsitem.headline: Photos show China has not beefed up Spratlys - Ramos.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos displayed pictures of the disputed Spratly Islands on national television on Wednesday to counter opposition claims that China had reinforced its presence in the area.

"Take a look...make your own conclusions," Ramos told a nationally televised news conference as aides held up pictures taken by Philippine reconnaissance planes between February 1995 and November this year.
The potentially oil-rich cluster of isles and reefs in the South China Sea is claimed wholly or in part by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
The photos of Mischief Reef in the Spratlys showed metal structures the Chinese have built and which Manila says could become naval support facilities.
Beijing, which has refused to dismantle them, says they are shelters for fishermen.

Ramos ordered the pictures shown after opposition senator Blas Ople last week said that while Ramos was having a pleasure cruise on Manila Bay with visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin, China was beefing up its Spratlys structures.
During the cruise, Ramos and Jiang danced and sang American songs like the late rock star Elvis Presley's "Love Me Tender."

"We don't want to assail anybody here but for the good of this country, I think we should sing more songs to each other as Filipinos in the most harmonious way and to our foreign friends and neighbours as romantically as possible," Ramos said.
Ramos and Jiang agreed during their Manila talks to shelve differences over the Spratlys and consider cooperation in developing the area.
